facts.claim: Chronic aircraft noise exposure was not associated with mental health problems and raised cortisol secretion in children.
facts.quote: Chronic aircraft noise was not associated with mental health problems and raised cortisol secretion.

facts.claim: Chronic exposure to industrial noise can lead to a change in pattern of salivary cortisol secretion especially in the evening, where an increase happened instead of its normal decrease.
facts.quote: This study showed that chronic exposure to industrial noise can lead to a change in pattern of salivary cortisol secretion especially in the evening (at the end of the work shift), in a way that instead of its normal decrease, an increase happened.
facts.causalWarning: causal wording, but the cited study only shows an association

facts.claim: Repeated exposure to motorboat noise for one and two weeks caused a diminished response in elevated ventilation rates in naïve fish.
facts.quote: We also found that naïve individuals responded to playback of motorboat noise with elevated ventilation rates, but that this response was diminished after one and two weeks of repeated exposure.

facts.claim: In a study of industrial workers, reducing noise intensity caused a significant reduction in reported fatigue (P < . 05) and postwork irritability (P < . 01).
facts.quote: There was also a concomitant reduction in reported fatigue (P < . 05) and postwork irritability (P < . 01).
facts.causalWarning: causal wording, but the cited study only shows an association

facts.claim: Chronic aircraft noise exposure is linked to higher levels of noise annoyance and poorer reading comprehension in school children.
facts.quote: Chronic aircraft noise exposure was associated with higher levels of noise annoyance and poorer reading comprehension measured by standardized scales with adjustments for age, deprivation and main language spoken.

facts.claim: No correlation was observed between urinary and hair cortisol in participants from the INMA-Sabadell cohort.
facts.quote: We observed no correlation between HCC and UCC in INMA-Sabadell participants, for whom both urinary and hair cortisol data were available.

research.angle: While chronic noise is linked to increased annoyance and altered cortisol patterns in some groups, it does not consistently cause elevated cortisol or mental health problems in children.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that noise impacts behavior, fatigue, and cortisol patterns differently depending on the population and duration of exposure.
research.caveat: Several studies found no statistically significant correlation between environmental noise and cortisol levels in children.
